title: permissions access: The access failure is caused by missing group role after migration.

transcript_turns.speaker: customer
transcript_turns.text: This is becoming a real blocker for us. customer reports symptoms consistent with more than one access issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: agent
transcript_turns.text: I need to follow the standard checklist before we discuss escalation. When did this first start?

transcript_turns.speaker: customer
transcript_turns.text: the issue began after a recent operational change

transcript_turns.speaker: agent
transcript_turns.text: That points me toward browser cache, but I want to keep this tentative. What changed right before the issue started?

transcript_turns.speaker: customer
transcript_turns.text: The confusing part is this: An early symptom seems to support browser cache, but later evidence weakens it.

transcript_turns.speaker: agent
transcript_turns.text: Let's test browser cache first. If that fits, we should see the same behavior on a known-good example.

transcript_turns.speaker: customer
transcript_turns.text: We checked one example and it seemed to fit, but then another example did not. customer reports symptoms consistent with more than one access issue, but at least one comparison case behaves differently.

transcript_turns.speaker: agent
transcript_turns.text: That weakens browser cache. I am going to abandon that path for now and check expired invitation.

transcript_turns.speaker: customer
transcript_turns.text: expired invitation happened to us once before, so that sounds plausible, but the symptoms are not exactly the same.

transcript_turns.speaker: agent
transcript_turns.text: Agreed. expired invitation is possible, but the evidence is mixed. I need a comparison between a working and blocked case.

transcript_turns.speaker: customer
transcript_turns.text: One working case has the same visible setup. Also, an admin later mentions missing group role after migration.

transcript_turns.speaker: agent
transcript_turns.text: That reverses the direction. The visible setup may not be the control point. I want to inspect the shared configuration boundary.

transcript_turns.speaker: customer
transcript_turns.text: I just got a note from someone else: logs show a warning that was initially dismissed. customer has a time-sensitive rollout or business deadline and trust is degrading.

transcript_turns.speaker: agent
transcript_turns.text: That late detail finally makes the actual path coherent. The likely root cause is: The access failure is caused by missing group role after migration.

transcript_turns.speaker: customer
transcript_turns.text: So the earlier checks were not wasted, but they were pointing at the wrong control point?

transcript_turns.speaker: agent
transcript_turns.text: Correct. The earlier paths were plausible but abandoned after conflicting evidence. Final outcome: agent identifies missing group role after migration as the likely operational cause, but certainty depends on the selected resolution type
